model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and coverage for different language model configurations. The x-axis represents the number of completions (k), displayed on a logarithmic scale (base 2) ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸, with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis represents coverage, displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.4 to 0.8. Four lines are shown, corresponding to different model variants: Llama-3B (dark green with cross/star markers), Llama-3B + FT (medium green with diamond-like markers), Llama-1B (light blue with circular markers), and Llama-1B + FT (darker blue with circular markers). The Llama-3B line begins near approximately 0.35–0.4 at 2⁰ completions, rises to a peak of roughly 0.55–0.6 around 2⁴ to 2⁵ completions, and then gradually declines toward approximately 0.5 at 2⁸. The Llama-3B + FT line follows a similar trajectory, starting around 0.35–0.4, peaking near 0.5–0.55 around 2⁴ to 2⁵, and declining slightly thereafter. The Llama-1B line starts at approximately 0.35 at 2⁰, rises to a peak around 0.45–0.5 near 2³ to 2⁴, and then declines to approximately 0.4 at 2⁸. The Llama-1B + FT line shows a similar pattern, starting near 0.35, reaching a modest peak around 0.45 near 2³ to 2⁴, and declining toward approximately 0.4 at 2⁸. All four lines exhibit a general pattern of initial increase followed by a gradual decrease at higher numbers of completions, with the 3B model variants generally achieving higher coverage values than the 1B variants across the range.
